A1.justification: Both PDFs describe ArtFormer. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and complete supplementary materials are readable and support reliable comparison, including matching relocated content.

before.justification: v1 reports original articulated-object generation experiments, baseline comparisons, human-study results, ablations, and supplementary editing and image-conditioning examples.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments and adds shape-prior and codebook comparisons plus quantitative text-alignment results.

M1.justification: The proposed tree-token transformer, four-codebook diffusion shape prior, tree position embedding, iterative decoding, and training objectives remain unchanged. Expanded explanations and renamed embedding modules clarify the existing method; the additional configurations are experimental comparison variants.

E1.justification: Both versions retain PartNet and PartNet-Mobility, text- and image-conditioned generation, object editing, and real-photograph examples. v2 explicitly names six training categories, but this supplies previously unspecified coverage details rather than establishing added or removed categories.

E2.justification: v2 adds Ours-NAPSP to Table 1 and Figure 5 and introduces the single-codebook variant. Figure 5 also newly includes CAGE and Ours-PR, which were already evaluated numerically in v1. Existing numerical comparators remain.

E3.justification: Supplement Sec. 7.4 introduces CLIP-R@10 evaluation using closed-state snapshots and CLIP ViT-L/14. New controlled configurations substitute NAP's shape prior or use one codebook. Existing ID, POR, human-study protocols, and training budgets remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v2 adds a single-versus-four-codebook ablation and an NAP-shape-prior comparison, probing codebook capacity and the shape prior's contribution. Existing component ablations, attention analysis, and editing examples remain. The novel-shape analysis moves to supplementary Sec. 7.1 without being newly introduced.

E5.justification: Repeated-run, seed, and uncertainty-reporting practices do not change. The human study retains 20 participants and the same task counts. Neither version supplies confidence intervals or significance tests for the benchmark comparisons; the added results are point estimates.

E6.justification: Existing numerical rows in Tables 1–2 are unchanged. v2 adds Ours-NAPSP and single-codebook results; Table 3 reports CLIP-R@10 of 0.2198 for Ours, 0.1429 for CAGE, 0.1648 for NAP-128, and 0.1319 for NAP-768. Figure 5 replaces NAP-768 examples and adds comparison outputs. The single-codebook results improve POR/MMD slightly but worsen COV/1-NNA relative to Full.

T1.justification: v2 corrects Gumbel-Softmax normalization from D terms in v1 Eq. (4) to N codebook entries in v2 Eq. (5). Distance-matrix and tree-path expressions are reorganized and clarified; these do not introduce a new proof or fundamentally different formulation.

C1.justification: The abstract is unchanged, and the introduction's three contributions and conclusion retain the same claims about controllable, diverse, high-quality articulated-object generation. Additional experimental support does not redefine the central contribution.

C2.justification: v2 newly reports declining geometry quality when training covers more object categories, tentatively attributing this to limited SDF generalization and suggesting alternatives. It also refines the anticipated advantage for objects with more than ten varying parts and the difficulty of capturing quantitative joint details.

D1.justification: v2 adds a code-repository link, identifies the six training categories, and specifies 64-dimensional absolute and 1024-dimensional tree position embeddings. It documents the CLIP model and snapshot setting for the new evaluation. Existing optimizer, hardware, batch-size, and training-duration information is retained.

R1.justification: v2 adds MeshArt, GenSDF, 3D Gaussian Splatting, and Park et al.'s compositional text-to-image benchmark. GRAINS replaces ATISS in Sec. 2.2, and attribution of the tree encoding becomes more explicit. These are focused updates to related work and research positioning.

P1.justification: v2 makes targeted language and explanation edits, renames Tokenizer/Untokenizer to Embedding Mapper/Unmapper, updates author affiliations, and adds acknowledgements. Novel Shape Generation moves from Sec. 4.4 to supplementary Sec. 7.1. The overall narrative structure remains recognizable.

P2.justification: Figure 5 expands from three to seven comparison rows, Tables 1–2 gain rows, and Table 3 is added. Figures 2–3 receive diagram edits, and v1 Figure 6 moves to supplementary Figure 10. Rebuttal changes are color-highlighted; the existing supplementary example images are retained.

improvement.justification: v2 strengthens evaluation through additional shape-prior/codebook controls and an automated text-alignment measure alongside the retained human study. The equation correction, implementation disclosures, and explicit category-scaling limitation improve clarity and transparency. These are incremental gains: the single-codebook results are mixed, and closed-state CLIP evaluation provides limited evidence about articulation-specific alignment.
